messages:
carla: Heads up — prepping a short playbook for GCP Cloud KMS in Private deployments. Need: minimum SA permissions, keyring/location guidance, rotation recommendations, audit log setup, and a clear envelope-encryption flow. Anyone with a recent checklist? :eyes:

alice: I wrote a draft last sprint. Minimal approach we shipped: create key ring in the same region as the private control plane, grant a dedicated service account only the cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter role on the specific key, and enable Data Access audit logs for cloudkms.googleapis.com.

ben: Agree. Important notes: use a dedicated SA per customer/environment (no shared SA), grant permissions at key level (not project) where possible, and prefer Workload Identity Federation if deploying off-GCP to avoid long-lived JSON keys.

carla: Can you paste the exact gcloud commands you used?

alice: Sure — trimmed example we put in the runbook:

```
# create key ring
gcloud kms keyrings create redwood-private-kr --location=us-central1
# create symmetric key with rotation (90d)
gcloud kms keys create redwood-dek --location=us-central1 --keyring=redwood-private-kr --purpose=encryption --rotation-period=7776000s
# bind encrypter/decrypter to service account
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding redwood-dek --location=us-central1 --keyring=redwood-private-kr --member=serviceAccount:sa-private-kms@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
```

alice: Note: rotation-period is in seconds; 7776000s = 90 days. We also leave an ops token creator role out of this SA — it only needs encryption/decryption.

ryan: For Private (VPC) deployments we also run KMS requests through the control plane network egress with a narrow firewall and use VPC-SC service perimeter where required. If you need strict exfil protection, put the key in a project inside the perimeter and restrict binding.

carla: Envelope encryption flow — succinct description?

alice: Envelope flow we documented:
1) App/runtime generates a random DEK (AES-256) per object or session.
2) App encrypts payload locally with DEK.
3) App calls KMS Encrypt API to wrap (encrypt) the DEK with the customer key, store wrapped_DEK alongside the ciphertext.
4) On read, app calls KMS Decrypt to unwrap DEK, then decrypts the payload locally.

alice: Important implementation points: cache unwrapped DEKs in memory very short-lived (e.g., 5–30s) and include TTL tied to key rotation events. Do not persist unwrapped DEKs to disk. Use AEAD (GCM) for payload encryption and include associated metadata (key version id) so you can choose correct KMS key version on decrypt.

ben: Rotation wise: use KMS automatic rotation for key versions, but apps must be key-version aware. When a key rolls, new Encrypt calls use the new primary version; Decrypt can still accept older versions. Update local metadata after successful rotate. Test rotation by creating a new version: `gcloud kms keys versions create --key=redwood-dek --keyring=redwood-private-kr --location=us-central1` and then set it primary.

carla: Audit logging requirements?

dave: We require Data Access logs for KMS at org-level export to our audit project for 1y retention. Enable these logs: cloudkms.googleapis.com activity (ADMIN_READ/ADMIN_WRITE) and Data Access (ENCRYPT/DECRYPT). In GCP console set Logging -> Logs Router -> sink to bigquery or pubsub for SIEM ingestion. Also tag entries with request metadata (requester SA, key name, key version).

carla: Any RBAC pitfalls or gotchas?

alice: A few we've hit:
- Granting roles at project level accidentally gives SA access to other keys. Always bind to the key resource if possible.
- Using broad roles like cloudkms.admin on a SA used by runtime — too powerful. Keep SA minimal.
- Forgetting to enable Data Access logs (they're disabled by default for KMS) so you end up with no decrypt events in audit.

ben: Also watch IAM conditions if you need time-of-day or IP-based restrictions. And if using SA impersonation, grant iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator only to the principals that truly need it.

carla: Operational checklist we can paste into runbook?

alice: Short checklist (copyable):
- [ ] Create key ring in same region as control plane
- [ ] Create symmetric key with rotation policy (90d or per compliance)
- [ ] Create dedicated SA per env/customer
- [ ] Grant roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on key to SA
- [ ] Avoid broad roles at project/org level
- [ ] Enable Data Access + Admin audit logs for cloudkms.googleapis.com and export to audit project
- [ ] Use Workload Identity Federation for off-gcp hosts or short-lived JSON keys if not possible
- [ ] Implement envelope encryption with short-lived DEK caching and key-version metadata
- [ ] Test rotate: create new version, ensure decrypt of old ciphertexts succeeds
- [ ] Record key rotation events in ops timeline and alert on failed decrypts

ops-bot: Reminder: runbook created at https://confluence.redwood.internal/kms/private-playbook (draft), tagging #eng-security for review. :robot_face:

carla: Perfect — I'll fold this into the Private deployment security runbook and flag for review. If anyone wants to add specific org-policy or VPC-SC snippets, drop them here and I'll include. Thanks! :v:
